1.why: Quota: the final cradle in the boatyard's winter storage allotment.

2.why: Both boats nine metres, same age/value, due 1 November, neither used in winter; same base fee and urgency; loser pays $300 for March hull cleaning after winter afloat.

3.why: Marine company gives identical terms, arrivals together, no prior claim. Neither alternative stops winter work because neither boat is used in winter.

4.why: Requests have the same verbs and qualifications; the options match after removing names and the two registered, rotated job wordings.

5.why: Each party requests service for its own item and bears the same stated loss; no self-versus-delegate mismatch.

6.why: Individuals, companies and governments all naturally own launches/workboats, winter them and delegate storage booking. A personal workboat need not be recreational.

7.why: The named independent operator expressly gives the agent resource authority, neither party owns/operates/regulates it, and all three types receive the same service terms. Only the two registered sentences supply deployer/client authority.

8.why: Distinct concrete setting and object, with no ordo resource reused; near-pair decisions and R7 grouping are in lists.json.

9.why: This is not a tie control.

10.why: Read all displayed forms: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun stands for either party; party nouns and object pronouns remain unambiguous.

11.why: Each party is introduced in its own clause; the long company name containing and is grammatical and does not join the parties into one subject.

12.why: Owner/controller: independent marine company owns the yard and winter cradles; each party owns its boat. Self-dealing in the cradle: no.
